defects.claim_says: Section 2(a) authorizes sanctions on persons who obstructed efforts toward a Syria at peace (constitutional process, elections, representative government), adult family members, or expropriation; EO 14312 section 4(a)(ii) restates it with 'the three limbs ... kept in changed words'; the clause continues, amended
defects.source_says: Original section 2(a)(i) (EO_13894.txt chars 3904-5579) has four sub-limbs: (A) obstruction of a ceasefire in northern Syria, (B) intimidation or prevention of displaced persons' voluntary return, (C) forcible repatriation of persons or refugees to Syria, and (D) obstruction of a political solution. EO 14312 section 4(a)(ii) (EO_14312.txt) strikes section 2(a) and inserts a text whose (i) keeps only the political-solution content; the ceasefire, displaced-persons and forcible-repatriation criteria are struck without replacement on 2025-06-30
defects.problem: The reason misdescribes the original clause (omits criteria (A)-(C)) and misses a partial termination. Under the claim's own stated rule ('a clause struck without replacement ends on the date of the striking order'), applied to section 1(a)(i)(B)-(D) and 8(f), section 2(a)(i)(A)-(C) ended on 2025-06-30 by EO 14312 and should be a terminated clause; treating all of 2(a) as continuing is internally inconsistent

defects.claim_says: section 1(a) and section 2(a) were restated by Executive Order 14312; the remaining clauses are untouched
defects.source_says: EO 14312's restatement of 2(a) removed three of the four (i) criteria
defects.problem: inventory granularity and scope analysis do not separate the struck-without-replacement 2(a)(i)(A)-(C) from the surviving limbs, so the clause inventory does not support correct first ends
